texts.preamble: Ramesh Chandra Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2018 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-21419-2016 (Ramesh Chandra Jain Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) 11 Jabalpur, Dated : 20-02-2018
texts.facts: a hy 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the authorized Food Inspector obtained a sample of food item 'mawa' (dry milk) from ad Ashirwad Mawa Kendra. The petitioner is the proprietor of Ashirwad M Mawa Kendra. On 12.10.2009, after observing all necessary formalities, the Food Inspector obtained the sample of 'mawa'. One of of the sample was sent for analysis to the State Food Laboratory. The rt other two parts were deposited before the Local Health Officer. On ou 28.10.2009, the food item sent was found to be adulterated. Prosecution was launched against the petitioner for violation of C sections 7(i), 7(iii) read with section 16(1)(a) of the Food Adulteration h Act, 1954 [hereinafter referred to as the "Act of 1954"] and Rule 50 of ig Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 [for short "Rules of H 1955"]. 3. On 10.1.2012 the petitioner-accused appeared before the trial Court. He moved an application for sending the second sample to the Central Food Laboratory on 30.1.2012. The sample was sent on 26.3.2012. Report dated 22.9.2016 was received, in which, it is contended that the food item has been found to be putrefied and not fit for examination. Therefore, the petitioner claimed that he was deprived of the provision under section 13(2) of the Act of 1954. The petitioner also claimed that the prosecution did not file the criminal case in time. The second sample could not be sent for examination to the Central Food Laboratory within time. However, when the second sample was sent for examination in the Central Food Laboratory, it was found that a the sample is unfit for examination.
texts.arguments: It is contended that milk products, as food items, are not fit for analysis after 10 months from the date of obtaining sample. It is contended that purpose of section 13(2) of the Act of 1954 has been defeated claiming that it is a case of no evidence. The petitioner claims that further proceeding in this regard would be abuse of process of the Court. Ramesh Chandra Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88636871/ 1 4. On behalf of the respondent/State the petition is vehemently opposed and it is contended that the delay was caused by the petitioner himself and, therefore, he cannot take advantage of his own mistake. ad 6. The petitioner's claim seems to be reasonable as the M second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory on 26.3.2012, which is after about two and half years. It is observed that the milk of products gets deteriorated within 10 months from the date of collection, therefore, holding because of delay in the institution of the rt complainant, the valuable right of the petitioner has been infringed. ou 7. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Municipal C Corporation of Delhi vs. Ghisaram, AIR 1967 SC 970 and in the case h of State of Harayana vs. Unique Farmaid P. Ltd. and others, AIR ig 2000 SCW 1985 has observed that the complaint filed as late as 19 H months and for this delay prosecution cannot thrust blame on the petitioner. 8. In the case of Ghisaram (supra) the same was sent after 19 months and, therefore, it was observed by the Apex Court that the accused has a right to apply under section 13(2) of the Act of 1954. In similar legal and factual circumstances, as available in of the present case, in the case of Suresh Narain vs. Food Inspector and another, 2003 (2) MPLJ 120 the proceedings of criminal case pending rt before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Indore was [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Similar ou finding has also been given in the case of Ravindra Agrawal vs. State C of Madhya Pradesh [M.Cr.C.No.4392/2017 decided on 20.9.2017].
